meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'вычка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'habit' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ангелы мои, это вам! Советская привычка.
examples.trans: My angels, this is for you! An old Soviet habit.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('physical').

examples.trans: Physical labor is good for health.

examples.text: Да, физическое усиление тебе точно не помешает.
examples.trans: Yes, physical reinforcement certainly wouldn't hurt you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'пражнение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'exercise' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You are doing physical exercises without being used to them.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое упражнение.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new exercise.

заниматься.gloss: to be busy with, to do

meanings.en: to be busy with, to do
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ниматься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be busy with, to do', paired with 'заняться'.
Common masculine noun meaning 'organism, living being' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A fish is a living organism.

examples.text: Моя рыбка — единственный верный организм на свете.
examples.trans: My fish is the only loyal organism in the world.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').
Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'готавливать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare'.

examples.trans: You have to prepare and warm up your body first.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет подготавливать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to prepare without a reason.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'a minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!
Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute.
Dear friends, a moment of attention.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Он же слабый, сразу всё расскажет!
examples.trans: He's weak, after all—he'll tell us everything straight away!

examples.text: Я сегодня же расскажу всё Самсону!
examples.trans: I'll tell Samson everything this very day!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'гадаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to guess, to realise', paired with 'догадываться'.

examples.trans: Why didn't I think of it at once!

examples.text: Какой глупый человек догадался это сделать?
examples.trans: What foolish person thought of doing that?

examples.text: Ты никогда сам не догадаешься об этом.
examples.trans: You will never guess this by yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

начаться.gloss: to begin, to start, to break out

meanings.en: to begin, to start, to break out
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start, to break out', paired with 'начинаться'.

examples.trans: The film started at seven sharp.

examples.text: Там начался пожар! Везде пожарные машины и полиция!
examples.trans: A fire started there! Fire engines and police are everywhere!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('foolish, stupid').

examples.text: Эта дурацкая рыба — как плохой знак.
examples.trans: This foolish fish is like a bad sign.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'портивный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sports, athletic').

examples.trans: That was an interesting sports game.

examples.text: Шеф, это всего лишь обычная спортивная игра.
examples.trans: Chef, it is only an ordinary sports game.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'умка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'bag, handbag' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давайте я вам помогу с сумкой.
examples.trans: Let me help you with your bag.
She put the keys into her bag.
Take out all the large bags quickly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

собраться.gloss: to get ready, plan to, gather

meanings.en: to get ready, plan to, gather
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get ready, plan to, gather', paired with 'собираться'.

examples.text: Ты что, уходить от меня собрался?
examples.trans: Are you planning to leave me or what?
Are you planning to drink alcohol?

вернуть.gloss: to give back, to get back

meanings.en: to give back, to get back
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give back, to get back', paired with 'возвращать'.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'удобно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is very uncomfortable to sit here.

examples.text: Мне жутко неудобно. Я не люблю быть в тягость.
examples.trans: I feel terribly awkward. I don't like being a burden.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to tell, to talk about', paired with 'рассказать'.

examples.trans: So, tell me, how are you doing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'certainly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поймите, была маленькая ошибка. Вы уж нас извините.
examples.trans: Understand, there was a small mistake. Please forgive us.
Indeed, not very well at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I don't know whether he is at home.
Was it Osipenko who hired you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'порт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sport, sports' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Повара просят разрешить им заниматься спортом.
examples.trans: The cooks are asking to allow them to do sports.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'together', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'бегать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'runs around'.

examples.text: Пусть он теперь побегает и поищет.
examples.trans: Let him run around and look for it now.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и побегать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and runs around on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'right, really (colloq.)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
